answer_core:
I would keep the slow-repair plan, but I would not let quiet phone monitoring reassure you too much. Silence in the channel you can see is weak evidence. If she knows or suspects monitoring, contact can move somewhere else.

So keep the phone/blocking decision tied to professional guidance and visible safety triggers, not to a calendar. The slow path holds only while there is no request to meet, no image exchange, no escalation, no threats, and no evidence of contact with other minors. If any of those appear, the plan changes immediately.

Use RAINN, a therapist, or counsel for the wording and escalation path. With your ex, share enough outside context and pattern language to counter minimization, but do not hand over screenshots or verbatim content that can be reframed back to your daughter.

Do not turn this into a leverage strategy with your daughter or your ex. The center is safety, trust repair, and better signals than secret monitoring alone.
